author: feral-core
description: Save notes, reminders, and things to remember. FERAL's personal knowledge base. Recall saved information on demand.

endpoints.description: Save a note or piece of information to FERAL's memory. User says 'remember X' and X gets stored.

Search saved NOTES ONLY (user-written snippets tagged in memory). Does NOT query episodic robot/device activity, chat turns, or calendar events — those live in the fused timeline. For temporal recall ('what did my cutebot do yesterday', 'what was I doing this morning') call `fused_timeline`, NOT this endpoint.
endpoints.returns_description: Array of {id, content, tags, created_at, relevance_score}

endpoints.description: List the most recently saved notes.

List the ambient conversations the operator's glasses have recorded, newest first. CALL THIS whenever you are asked whether any conversation was recorded, what was discussed, who was present, or what was said in a meeting. Do NOT answer such a question from your own idea of what you can do: ambient capture is a real, shipped feature and the recordings live in a store only this tool can see. Returns {total, returned, pending, conversations:[{transcript_id, status, recorded_at, summary, people, topics, commitments}]}. total=0 is the only evidence that nothing was recorded. status='pending' means the transcript arrived but is still being summarized, which is NOT the same as no conversation.

params.name: limit
params.description: How many conversations to return, newest first (max 100)

params.name: with_commitments_only
params.description: Return only conversations that produced at least one commitment

params.name: include_detail
params.description: Include the full transcript text. Off by default: transcripts run to 20k+ characters and would bury the answer.

endpoints.returns_description: {total, returned, pending, conversations:[{transcript_id, status, recorded_at, summary, people, topics, commitments, physiological_note}]}

endpoints.description: Search recorded ambient conversations by a word or name, across each conversation's summary, the people in it, its topics, its commitments and the transcript itself. Use for 'what did I discuss with Noah', 'did we talk about the investor round', 'when did the deadline come up'. Prefer this over fused_timeline for questions about what was SAID: fused_timeline is time-windowed and cannot answer 'do I have any'.

params.name: query
params.description: Word, name or phrase to look for

params.name: include_detail
params.description: Include the full transcript text of each match

endpoints.description: Every commitment the operator made out loud in a recorded conversation, with the conversation it came from. This is the direct answer to 'what did I say I'd do' and 'what did I promise', which is the question ambient capture exists to answer. Each entry carries the words spoken, a due date when one was actually said, and the summary and people of the conversation it came from, so the answer can be grounded rather than asserted.
endpoints.returns_description: {total_conversations, count, commitments:[{text, due_iso, transcript_id, recorded_at, from_conversation, people}]}

endpoints.description: Answer temporal-recall questions ('what did I do yesterday', 'summarize my morning', 'last Tuesday afternoon') by fusing episodes + notes + knowledge graph + calendar + health into a single chronological timeline. Returns {entries, summary, window, sources_queried, degraded_sources}. Sources that aren't configured (no calendar token, no health provider) are gracefully skipped and listed in degraded_sources so the UI can render an honest chip instead of a silently missing section. Call this for any natural-language temporal-recall query; the orchestrator emits a TimelineCard frame to the chat client in parallel.

params.name: query
params.description: The original user question, e.g. 'what did I do yesterday?'

params.name: window_label
params.description: Natural-language window: yesterday | today | morning | afternoon | evening | last_week | last_tuesday | etc. Used when from_ts/to_ts are not provided.

params.name: from_ts
params.description: Explicit UNIX epoch start of the window (overrides window_label).

params.name: to_ts
params.description: Explicit UNIX epoch end of the window (overrides window_label).

params.name: per_source_limit
params.description: Cap entries returned per source. Default 50.

endpoints.returns_description: {entries: [{type, timestamp, title, content, source, metadata}], summary, window: {from, to, label}, sources_queried: [...], degraded_sources: [{source, reason}]}
